hiro_menmen_kawaguchi.vegan_detail: The shop centers on meat-based ramen and tsukemen with chashu pork, and broths for ramen and dipping soup are animal-based. There is no documented vegan or vegetarian option.
hiro_menmen_kawaguchi.notes: [Mom & Pop] A small noodle shop that opened on December 3, 2024 on the second floor of a building in Nakamachi, central Hiroshima, a short walk east of Peace Memorial Park.

chef_bio.background: A small noodle shop that opened on December 3, 2024 on the second floor of a building in Nakamachi, central Hiroshima, a short walk east of Peace Memorial Park.
chef_bio.philosophy: The owner takes the noodles themselves seriously, sourcing lunch tsukemen noodles from Aichi and the evening miso ramen noodles from Hokkaido to suit each style of dish.
chef_bio.specialty: A two-faced noodle concept: at lunch the shop serves dipping-style tsukesoba, and at dinner it switches entirely to miso ramen, offering white, red, and black miso variations including a garlic miso butter bowl.

anecdotes.text: The lunch dipping noodles and the dinner miso ramen use different noodles sourced from different regions — Aichi for the lunch tsukemen and Hokkaido for the evening miso ramen.
The dual lunch-tsukemen, dinner-miso-ramen format gives regulars a reason to come back at different times of day to try both sides of the menu.

cultural_comfort.note: This is a small, casual owner-run noodle shop where ordering is straightforward; basic Japanese or pointing at the menu works well, but expect little to no English support.

hiro_bakkajin.gf_detail: The house specialty is wheat noodles made by the adjacent Harada Seimen, served in a soy-sauce broth (soy sauce contains wheat). This is a wheat-noodle shop with no gluten-free option.
hiro_bakkajin.vegan_detail: The cold noodles and tsukemen are built around a soy-sauce-based broth with pork chashu and other meat/fish-derived elements; no vegan offering is documented.
hiro_bakkajin.hours_raw: Tue/Thu/Sun/holidays 11:30-14:00; Wed/Fri/Sat 11:30-14:00 and 17:30-21:00; closed Monday; Sunday lunch served on alternating weeks only.
hiro_bakkajin.notes: [Mom & Pop] Opened September 2021 in the EBBA VILLAGE building right beside the Harada Seimen noodle factory in Eba Sakaemachi. It was started by a relative of the Harada Seimen family, with the storefront serving customers and rental units occupying the back of the building.

roles: family-run noodle shop tied to Harada Seimen
chef_bio.background: Opened September 2021 in the EBBA VILLAGE building right beside the Harada Seimen (原田製麺) noodle factory in Eba Sakaemachi. It was started by a relative of the Harada Seimen family and runs as a friendly, no-frills counter shop.
chef_bio.philosophy: Showcasing the family's own Harada Seimen noodles in a friendly, no-frills counter setting.
chef_bio.specialty: Hiroshima cold noodles made with Harada Seimen's own wheat noodles, plus evening izakaya fare

anecdotes.text: Reviewers note the broth runs intensely savory and soy-sauce-forward; when one diner found it too salty, the smiling staff repeatedly offered to add more spice rather than dilute it.
A bowl runs about 1,150 yen, roughly 350 yen cheaper than the noodles made from the same Harada Seimen supply served at the well-known Shinkaen.
Visitors describe the kitchen as run by a few cheerful women whose friendliness is part of the draw.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: oomin77 and h-megourmet confirm the Sept 2021 opening beside Harada Seimen in Eba Sakaemachi, the Harada-family tie, Hiroshima cold noodles made with Harada Seimen noodles (~1,150 yen, cheaper than Shinkaen which uses the same supply), a strong soy-forward broth, a night izakaya format, and cheerful female staff.

gf_cross_contamination.text: The entire menu centers on wheat noodles produced at the adjacent Harada Seimen factory, so the kitchen is a heavy wheat-flour environment.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The signature broth is described as intensely soy-sauce-forward; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Dishes are topped with pork chashu and served in a meat/fish-and-soy-based broth; no plant-only preparation is documented.

cultural_comfort.note: A small family-run noodle counter where ordering is straightforward but staff likely speak little English, so a few words of Japanese or pointing at the menu will help.

It operates as a small neighbourhood take-out bakery on a Tuesday–Saturday schedule (closed Sun/Mon). The owner-baker's name is not disclosed in available Japanese press or listings; the shop is present on Instagram as @theta.komekopan.

hiro_bigapple.gf_detail: [Held at "ask" 2026-08-20] The description below was not traceable to any source, so the GF label is held down until it is. A fully plant-based Indian cafe with a genuine wheat-free curry claim: local press reports the daily curry is made 小麦粉のルーを使わず (with no wheat-flour roux), thickened instead with an 11-spice blend and beans (soy/adzuki/kidney/lentil/chickpea) served with rice. The three cakes are described as グルテンフリー (chocolate, handmade-tofu cheesecake, daily pound cake). However the shared kitchen also turns out clearly wheat-bearing items — vegetable momo dumplings (wheat wrapper), soy-meat karaage (typically wheat/starch coating), tempeh fries and luorou rice (soy sauce = wheat) — so this is options, not dedicated. Falafel is chickpea-based but is fried and cross-contact with battered items in a shared fryer is likely; confirm rice+curry or the GF cakes and ask about tamari and the fryer.
hiro_bigapple.vegan_detail: [Held at "some vegan options" 2026-08-20] The "fully vegan" label was contradicted by this record's own cited sources. 100% vegan establishment — every item is animal-product-free per Vegewel and Tabelog (どのメニューも動物性不使用). Founder Guru Maiko built the menu around Indian vegetarian/vegan cooking; the tofu cheesecake uses handmade tofu 'cheese' and desserts are dairy-free. No meat, fish, egg or dairy on the menu.
hiro_bigapple.notes: [GF] Fully vegan cafe a short taxi ride (~5 min) or 25-min walk from the Miyajima ferry at Miyajimaguchi — a handy plant-based stop. Safest celiac order is the daily curry with rice (owner uses no wheat-flour roux, 11-spice blend + beans) or the gluten-free cakes/chai. Avoid the momo dumplings, luorou rice (soy sauce), and battered fried items; ask about the fryer for falafel and whether tamari can replace soy sauce. Small (14 seats), irregular hours and early closes — check the Instagram/LINE before going.

chef_bio.background: Owner Guru Maiko (reported age 39) discovered vegan cooking through yoga and travelled to India four times over about ten years, where she was struck by how flavourful meat-free food could be. She married an Indian man she met on her travels and opened Big Apple with her husband in spring 2023 in Ōno, Hatsukaichi. The white-themed, casual eatery-style cafe centres on Indian vegetarian/vegan home cooking. Contact is via a LINE official account and Instagram rather than a full website.
chef_bio.philosophy: 『肉がなくても、しっかり味がついたおいしい料理が食べられる』 — that meat-free food can be fully satisfying and richly seasoned.
chef_bio.specialty: Daily bean curry built on an 11-spice blend and no wheat roux; Indian-influenced vegan plates and gluten-free cakes.

anecdotes.text: The daily curry pairs a rotating bean (soy, adzuki, kidney, lentil or chickpea) with an 11-spice blend chosen to complement that day's bean, and uses no wheat-flour roux.
Maiko visited India four times across roughly a decade and opened the cafe with her Indian husband after being inspired by the country's vegetarian cooking.

hiro_cocoroba.gf_detail: A 100% rice-flour bread specialist that bakes no wheat at all. The shop's own site states 「国産米粉のみを使用し、余計な添加物を含まないグルテンフリーのおいしいパン生地作りに取り組みました」 and markets itself as a 「完全グルテンフリー米粉パン専門店」, using only domestic rice flour (Hiroshima Koshihikari + Kumamoto Mizuho Chikara blend). Curated GF guide komeko-palette confirms the facility 「小麦粉を一切使用していない」, eliminating cross-contact from equipment/utensils — no shared wheat line. Celiac-safe for the plain breads; note that cheese and chocolate varieties contain dairy (乳) though all items remain wheat- and egg-free.
hiro_cocoroba.vegan_detail: All breads are wheat- and egg-free, and many plain breads (e.g. 食パン, メロンパン) are also dairy-free and effectively vegan. However cheese and chocolate varieties contain dairy, and savory toasts use tuna (ツナ) and mentaiko (明太) fish roe, so not everything is plant-based. Ask which of the day's items are dairy- and fish-free.
hiro_cocoroba.hours_raw: 10:00–17:00 (closes when sold out); closed Wednesdays (open if a holiday)
hiro_cocoroba.notes: [GF-dedicated] A wheat-free rice-flour bakery — the whole facility uses only domestic rice flour, so there is no wheat line to cross-contaminate. Safe for celiacs for the plain breads; cheese/chocolate items add dairy and savory toasts add fish, so confirm your specific item is dairy/fish-free if that matters. Opens 10:00 and sells out, so go early.

chef_bio.background: CoCoRoBA opened in November 2022 in Toshimatsu, Saeki-ku, Hiroshima, as a dedicated gluten-free rice-flour bread shop. It was built around the three major food allergies (wheat, egg, dairy), aiming to give allergy sufferers and health-conscious customers bread they can eat with confidence. The owner sources only domestic rice flour — a blend of Hiroshima-grown Koshihikari and Kumamoto's Mizuho Chikara variety developed for rice bread — and uses moshio sea salt from Kami-Kamagari island and sudaki unrefined cane sugar (素焚糖) from Amami Oshima, avoiding unnecessary additives. The shop runs both a storefront and a nationwide online BASE shop.
chef_bio.philosophy: Bread that people with wheat, egg and dairy allergies can eat safely, made from carefully chosen domestic rice flour without unnecessary additives.
chef_bio.specialty: 100% rice-flour gluten-free breads (shokupan, melon pan, cream pan, savory toasts)

anecdotes.text: Uses a two-variety rice-flour blend — Hiroshima Koshihikari plus Kumamoto Mizuho Chikara — chosen for texture while keeping domestic sourcing.
The facility uses absolutely no wheat flour, fundamentally eliminating cross-contamination risk from equipment and utensils.

The shop's own site carries the first-party claim (page title 「完全グルテンフリー米粉パン専門店」 plus 「国産米粉のみを使用し…グルテンフリーのおいしいパン生地作りに取り組みました」 and 「3大食物アレルギー（小麦・卵・乳）の方や健康志向の方にも、安心してお召し上がりいただけます」), and two separate GF-specialist lists corroborate at FACILITY level: japan-glutenfree.com includes it under the criterion 「工房・店内に小麦粉を一切持ち込まず、すべての商品がグルテンフリー」, and komeko-palette states it does not use any wheat flour in manufacturing and has 'completely eliminated the risk of wheat contamination from manufacturing equipment or cooking utensils.' Four further independent Japanese sources (alleco, family-dr, mamanpere, nh-times) agree, family-dr noting all items carry allergy labelling; the shop is absent from japan-glutenfree's closed-shops register and is trading normally. No negative celiac report, no glutening account, and no evidence of wheat gluten being added exists.
red_flags: No third-party lab testing or ppm certification — the no-wheat-on-premises claim rests on the shop's word plus two GF-guide editors, not on assay
Cheese and chocolate varieties contain dairy (乳) — matters for the vegan label, not the GF one
Savory toasts (tuna, mentaiko-garlic) carry sauces/seasonings that were never itemised; wheat soy sauce cannot be ruled out on those specific items
Sells out and closes early; closed Wednesdays — trip risk, not a safety risk

hiro_koguma.gf_detail: A rare genuinely gluten-free HIROSHIMA-style okonomiyaki — the local wheat trap, since Hiroshima-yaki normally layers a wheat crêpe batter AND wheat soba/udon noodles. This 1970-founded shop developed a dedicated GF version (¥690) whose batter and noodles are wheat-free: the venue states 「小麦粉と小麦由来成分を含まない生地と麺を使っています」(uses batter and noodles containing no wheat flour or wheat-derived ingredients), and also offers a 7大アレルゲンフリー (seven-major-allergen-free, i.e. no wheat/egg/milk) type. CRITICAL cross-contact caveat: the shop cooks ordinary WHEAT okonomiyaki on the same teppan all day, so the GF/allergen-free versions are made to order and require phoning a reservation by the previous day (要予約) — discuss celiac needs and shared-grill risk when you book; kept at ASK for that reason.
hiro_koguma.vegan_detail: Okonomiyaki here is built on egg, pork and (for standard versions) bonito/sauce — not a vegan venue. No vegan options are advertised.
hiro_koguma.notes: [GF] Order the グルテンフリーお好み焼き (¥690) or the 7大アレルゲンフリー type — the batter and noodles are wheat-free, which is genuinely unusual for Hiroshima-yaki. You MUST reserve by the day before so they prep the GF batter/noodles; the same teppan also cooks wheat okonomiyaki, so explain celiac disease and ask about a cleaned/separated cooking area. Also does frozen nationwide mail-order of the GF version.

chef_bio.background: 仔ぐま was founded in 1970 (昭和45年) in Rakurakuen, Saeki-ku, a residential district of southwest Hiroshima, and is run by owner-chef Nakagawa Ken. It is a long-established neighbourhood Hiroshima-yaki shop that took the unusual step of developing allergen-conscious versions of its dish: a seven-major-allergen-free okonomiyaki launched in 2013, followed about two years later by a fully gluten-free version, and a low-carbohydrate version on 1 October 2017. The low-carb/allergen work was reported by local press and Otafuku Sauce's okonomiyaki column, and the shop even ran blood-glucose testing in cooperation with a hospital. The GF and low-carb lines are also sold frozen for nationwide delivery.
chef_bio.philosophy: Make Hiroshima's signature okonomiyaki accessible to people who normally cannot eat it — those with wheat/gluten intolerance, celiac disease, or diabetes — without giving up the layered Hiroshima-yaki form.
chef_bio.specialty: Gluten-free and seven-allergen-free Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki with wheat-free batter and noodles

The owner's stated goal is to make 「誰でも安心して食べられるおやつ」— snacks that anyone can eat with peace of mind, including people with allergies. The shop also ships nationwide, with free shipping over ¥4,500.
